citation: Raza et al. 2010, J. Nanosci. Nanotechnol. 10:1203

materials.notes: Fully characterized sample. Ce:Sm = 4:1 in solution -> SDC = Ce0.8Sm0.2O1.9 (confirmed by EDX). EDX gives final SDC:Na2CO3 molar ratio ~1:0.5 (surplus Na2CO3 remained; NaNO3 volatilizes at 800 C). Particle sizes: BET 14.5 nm, XRD 12.6 nm, TEM 14 nm. Cell: 13 mm diameter, 0.8 mm total thickness, 0.7 cm2 active area, sintered 650 C 30 min in air, H2/air, 80-120 mL/min, 1 atm. Also Pmax = 1000 mW/cm2 at 520 C. No direct conductivity, activation energy, OCV, or durability values reported.

Only XRD data reported (lattice parameter shown in Fig 2). No fuel-cell performance, conductivity, morphology or final composition analysis given for this sample. Excess Na2CO3 in synthesis = 0.15 mol (beyond the 1:1.5 needed for SDC precursor formation).
Only XRD data reported (lattice parameter). No fuel-cell performance, conductivity or morphology analysis given. Excess Na2CO3 in synthesis = 0.25 mol.

extraction_notes: Paper prepares three carbonate@SDC samples (Ce12, Ce13, Ce14) differing in the Na2CO3 excess used in synthesis, but focuses characterization and fuel cell testing on Ce12 only. Pmax values 1180 mW/cm2 (540 C) and 1000 mW/cm2 (520 C) are for the tested sample (implicitly Ce12; Fig 7 caption does not label the sample but only Ce12 is characterized in the results section and the paper says 'a specific composition of Carbonate@ceria... gives the best performances'). Ce13 and Ce14 have essentially no data beyond XRD lattice parameters -> mostly null. No conductivity, activation energy, OCV, relative density, or durability values in the paper. secondary_phase_wt_pct not stated as wt% (EDX gives SDC:Na2CO3 molar ratio ~1:0.5 for Ce12 only).
